newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower on slide in corn, soy.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower on slide in corn, soy.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled lower amid spillover pressure from CBOT corn and soybean futures, traders said.
CBOT corn and beans opened lower and stayed weak amid forecasts for beneficial rain in key U.S. Midwest growing regions.
Added pressure on wheat came late as soybeans fell to the day's lows and the August contract plunged the 30-cent-per-bushel daily limit.
KCBT wheat settled 4-1/2 to seven cents per bushel lower, with Sept down 6-1/2 cents at $3.41.

Traders said Benson-Quinn and Linnco sold a combined one million bushels of KCBT Sept wheat at the close. On the day, Linnco bought 1.4 million Sept and one million December, but also sold one million each of Sept and Dec.
Traders said E. D. & F. Man International bought 2.1 million Sept bushels and sold two million Sept. Farmers Commodities sold two million Sept.
The KCBT estimated Thursday's volume at 43.260 million bushels, down from 54.320 million Tuesday.
